text:
Predicates:
Winner(x, y) ::: x is the winner of y.
Participated(x, y) ::: x participated in y.
Tie(x, y) ::: x is in a y-way tie.
From(x, y) ::: x is from y.
Leaderboard(x, y) ::: x is on the leaderboard of y.
Premises:
Winner(steinhauer, duMaurierClassic1992) ::: The winner of the 1992 du Maurier Classic was Steinhauer.
Participated(steinhauer, duMaurierClassic1992) ::: Steinhauer participated in the 1992 du Maurier Classic.
∃x (Tie(x, six) ∧ Leaderboard(x, duMaurierClassic1992)) ::: There was one six-way tie on the leaderboard and one person in the six-way tie was from Belgium.
From(descampe, belgium) ∧ Leaderboard(descampe, duMaurierClassic1992) ::: Descampe is from Belgium and is on the leaderboard of the 1992 du Maurier Classic.
∀x (Leaderboard(x, duMaurierClassic1992) → Participated(x, duMaurierClassic1992)) ::: All people on the leaderboard of the 1992 du Maurier Classic participated in the 1992 du Maurier Classic.
Conclusion:
¬Winner(steinhauer, duMaurierClassic1992) ::: Steinhauer was not the winner of the 1992 du Maurier Classic.
